findings.explanation: PowerNet-MIB has no object named upsLastTransferReason. The reason for the last transfer to battery is upsAdvInputLineFailCause (.1.3.6.1.4.1.318.1.1.1.3.2.5), an enumeration: noTransfer(1), highLineVoltage(2), brownout(3), blackout(4), smallMomentarySag(5), deepMomentarySag(6), and so on. The same wrong name appears in implementation and detailedImplementation, so a reader cannot configure the poll.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace upsLastTransferReason with upsAdvInputLineFailCause in dataSources, implementation and detailedImplementation, and list its enumeration values.

findings.explanation: The transfer-cause object is a polled scalar that holds the cause of the most recent transfer. It never increments, and it keeps its value after power returns, so it cannot count events. upsBasicOutputStatus is likewise a polled enumeration (onLine(2), onBattery(3), onSmartBoost(4), onSmartTrim(12)), not a bit field carried in traps. Transfer events reach the trap path as APC enterprise traps such as upsOnBattery.
findings.quote: or when `upsLastTransferReason` increments on the trap path. Decode `upsBasicOutputStatus` when traps expose on-battery bits
findings.suggested_fix: Detect a transfer by polling upsBasicOutputStatus=3 (onBattery), or by watching upsAdvInputLineFailCause change between polls, or by matching the APC upsOnBattery / powerRestored traps. Say which of these the SPL uses.

findings.explanation: With Splunk Connect for SNMP, Gauge values such as upsAdvInputLineVoltage go to the metrics index (default netmetrics) as sourcetype sc4snmp:metric, and traps arrive as sc4snmp:traps in the event index. Neither lands as snmp:apc:ups or snmp:trap in index=power, so the event search finds nothing on the SC4SNMP path.
findings.quote: standardize `sourcetype=snmp:apc:ups` for scheduled walks and optionally merge parallel trap streams carrying UPS MIB OIDs under `sourcetype=snmp:trap`
findings.suggested_fix: Document the real SC4SNMP sourcetypes and indexes (sc4snmp:metric in a metrics index queried with mstats; sc4snmp:traps in the event index), or restrict the snmp:apc:ups event sourcetype to SNMP Modular Input (1537) collection.

findings.explanation: The implementation and detailedImplementation describe a nominal-voltage lookup and a two-consecutive-poll persistence rule, but the SPL hard-codes 108/132 V and fires on a single low reading. On 230 V fleets every poll exceeds 132 V and alerts.
findings.quote: Normalize nominal voltage using lookup `ups_nominal_voltage` keyed on `host`. For North American 120 V service, alert when `upsAdvInputLineVoltage` stays below 108 V across two SNMP polls
findings.suggested_fix: Either state that the SPL is 120 V-only and fires on a single poll below 108 V, or describe the lookup-driven thresholds and two-poll rule as an extension the reader must add.

findings.explanation: The SPL searches only sourcetype=snmp:apc:ups. The trap sourcetype is never referenced, so trap-only transfer events are not detected.
findings.suggested_fix: List only snmp:apc:ups, or say that the trap stream needs a separate search or an append.

findings.explanation: Steps 2, 3 and 5 are generic template text: data model validation and tstats advice for a UC with no cimModels, and exception keys such as user, src and process_name. None of it applies to UPS voltage telemetry.
findings.quote: Confirm CIM field extractions resolve by running `| datamodel <model> search | head 1` and inspecting the relevant fields.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace these steps with UPS-specific validation: compare upsAdvInputLineVoltage against the NMC web UI, trigger a self-test (upsAdvInputLineFailCause=selfTest(9)) to prove the transfer path, and remove the CIM data model step.

findings.explanation: 'Harmonic-only monitoring classes' is undefined, and it is unclear which assets this excludes or why.
findings.quote: harmonic-only monitoring classes until battery-transfer SNMP OIDs are confirmed for those assets
findings.suggested_fix: Name the concrete asset types, for example power-quality meters that report voltage but have no transfer-to-battery capability.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: `match(toString(reason), "(?i)transfer|battery|boost|trim")` matches the idle value 'noTransfer' when the enumeration is rendered as text, so every healthy UPS counts as a transfer event. If the value arrives as an integer (1-10), the regex matches nothing. Because upsAdvInputLineFailCause holds the last cause indefinitely, a non-idle value also re-fires on every poll after a single transfer. Compare against an explicit list of enumeration values and detect a change, or use upsBasicOutputStatus=3.

`coalesce(upsLastTransferReason, transfer_reason)` references a non-existent PowerNet object (the real one is upsAdvInputLineFailCause), and the fixed 108/132 V thresholds cause continuous alerts on 230 V UPS units.
The title promises correlation of a voltage sag with transfer-to-battery events, but the SPL ORs the two conditions independently and never correlates them.

summary: The UC names a PowerNet-MIB object that does not exist (upsLastTransferReason; the real object is upsAdvInputLineFailCause) and misdescribes how transfer-cause and output-status values behave. The implementation promises nominal-voltage normalization and two-poll persistence that the SPL does not do, and the SPL's transfer regex matches the idle value 'noTransfer'.
